title: Extract a checkout notifier port
summary: Route checkout confirmations through an injected notifier port and enforce the order rules at the boundary.
objectives: Route a delivery detail through an explicit port instead of a concrete gateway.
Keep the checkout rule independent of the notification mechanism.
Enforce validation order at the boundary.
Make the send behavior observable without touching console output.
constraints: Keep the public types Order and INotifier, and the Checkout.Complete signature.
Never write to the console or call a static gateway from checkout.
Validate in this order: empty order, invalid recipient, below threshold.
Send exactly one message only when the order qualifies.
Use the message format Order {id} confirmed: {total} cents.
Return sent, empty_order, invalid_recipient, or below_threshold.

examples.output: sent, then notifier receives "Order 42 confirmed: 5000 cents"
examples.explanation: The threshold is inclusive, so 5000 qualifies.

examples.output: below_threshold, and the notifier receives nothing
examples.explanation: The checkout rules run before any delivery side effect.

public.name: Qualifying orders
public.description: A qualifying order sends exactly one confirmation through the port.

public.name: Rejected orders
public.description: Below-threshold and empty orders never reach the notifier.

hidden.name: Validation precedence

hidden.name: No duplicate sends

criteria.title: Port boundary
criteria.description: Checkout depends on the INotifier port and never on a concrete delivery mechanism or console.

criteria.title: Rule order
criteria.description: Validation order and result codes follow the contract, including precedence when several rules fail.

criteria.title: Behavior preservation
criteria.description: Qualifying orders send exactly one message with the exact required text.

criteria.title: Testability
